note: Pediatric cohorts show an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction phenotype centered on progressive microcephaly and synaptic proteostasis, while fetal cohorts ascertain on diverse structural anomalies where PLAA variants may be incidental or VUS.

evidence.text: PLAA mutations were shown to cause an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction syndrome characterized by progressive microcephaly, seizures, and disruption of endolysosomal trafficking of synaptic proteins without intrinsic structural organ malformations.

source.title: PLAA mutations cause a lethal infantile epileptic encephalopathy by disrupting ubiquitin-mediated endolysosomal degradation of synaptic proteins
source.quote: In both human and mouse, hypomorphic mutations in the ubiquitin adaptor protein PLAA cause an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction syndrome with seizures. Resulting from perturbed endolysosomal degradation, Plaa mutant neurons accumulate K63-polyubiquitylated proteins and synaptic membrane proteins, disrupting synaptic vesicle recycling and neurotransmission.

evidence.text: In a deceased fetal cohort evaluated by WES for ultrasound abnormalities including skeletal and genitourinary defects, compound heterozygous variants in PLAA were identified in association with neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies (NDMSBA).

source.title: Whole-exome sequencing in deceased fetuses with ultrasound anomalies: a retrospective analysis
source.quote: The most common ultrasound abnormalities were skeletal system abnormalities 39.2% (11/28), followed by multiple system abnormalities (17.9%, 5/28) and genitourinary abnormalities (17.9%, 5/28).
